facts.statement: Ichthyosaurus is an extinct genus of ichthyosaurs that lived during the Early Jurassic period in Europe, including Belgium, England, Germany, and Portugal.
facts.quote: Ichthyosaurus (derived from Greek ἰχθύς (ichthys) meaning 'fish' and σαῦρος (sauros) meaning 'lizard') is an extinct genus of ichthyosaurs from the Early Jurassic (Hettangian - Pliensbachian) of Europe (Belgium, England, Germany and Portugal).

facts.statement: The name Ichthyosaurus was first coined by Charles Konig in 1818, but it was not formally described until later.
facts.quote: The name Ichthyosaurus was first used by Charles Konig in 1818, but it was not used in a formal scientific description

facts.statement: Henry Beche and William Conybeare formally described the species Ichthyosaurus communis in 1821, establishing taxonomic priority over earlier names like Proteosaurus.
facts.quote: Henry Beche and William Conybeare in 1821 considered Ichthyosaurus to have taxonomic priority over Proteosaurus and named the species I. communis

facts.statement: The type species I. communis reached up to 2 meters in length, while other species varied, with I. larkini up to 2.5 meters, I. anningae up to 1.8 meters, I. breviceps up to 1.9 meters, and I. conybeari up to 1.5 meters.
facts.quote: I. communis reaching up to 2 m in length, I. larkini probably up to 2.5 m, I. anningae up to 1.8 m, I. breviceps up to 1.9 m, and I. conybeari up to 1.5 m.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence of babies inside adults indicates that Ichthyosaurus was viviparous, giving birth to live young.
facts.quote: Some fossils still had baby specimens inside them, indicating that Ichthyosaurus was viviparous.

facts.statement: Ichthyosaurus possessed a fleshy dorsal fin on its back and a large caudal fin.
facts.quote: Jurassic ichthyosaurs had a fleshy dorsal fin on their back as well as a large caudal fin.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Ichthyosaurus was a ram feeder incapable of suction feeding, relying on its jaws and teeth alone to capture prey.
facts.quote: Ichthyosaurus is suggested to have been a ram feeder, with the morphology of its hyobranchial apparatus suggesting that it was incapable of suction feeding, using the jaws and teeth alone to capture prey.

facts.statement: Three pregnant female specimens of Ichthyosaurus are known, all belonging to the subspecies I. somersetensis.
facts.quote: Three pregnant females are known, all of the subspecies I. somersetensis.

facts.statement: Although birth orientation is unclear, it is likely that Ichthyosaurus fetuses exited tail-first, a common trait in highly aquatic vertebrates.
facts.quote: Although none of the fetuses show a clear birth orientation it is likely they exited tail-first, a common feature in highly aquatic vertebrates.

facts.statement: The solid bones of Ichthyosaurus ears likely transferred water vibrations to the inner ear.
facts.quote: Los huesos del oído de Ichthyosaurus eran sólidos, probablemento transfiriendo las vibraciones del agua al oído interno.

facts.statement: Coprolites of Ichthyosaurus reveal that its diet consisted of fish and squids.
facts.quote: Coprolitos de Ichthyosaurus revelan que su dieta consistía de peces y calamares.

facts.statement: Ichthyosaurus is among the best-known ichthyosaur genera and serves as the type genus for the order Ichthyosauria.
facts.quote: It is among the best known ichthyosaur genera, as it is the type genus of the order Ichthyosauria.

facts.statement: Known species of Ichthyosaurus include I. communis (1822), I. breviceps (1881), I. conybeari (1888), I. anningae (2015), I. larkini (2017), and I. somersetensis (2017).
facts.quote: Ichthyosaurus communis (Beche and Conybeare, 1822) Ichthyosaurus breviceps (Owen, 1881) Ichthyosaurus conybeari (Lydekker, 1888) Ichthyosaurus anningae (Lomax and Massare, 2015) Ichthyosaurus larkini (Lomax and Massare, 2017) Ichthyosaurus somersetensis (Lomax and Massare, 2017)

facts.statement: It is debated how many valid species of Ichthyosaurus exist, as over 50 were attributed to the genus by 1900 before many were moved to separate genera or synonymized.
facts.quote: During the 19th century, almost all fossil ichthyosaurs were attributed to Ichthyosaurus, resulting in the genus having over 50 species by 1900. These species were subsequently moved to separate genera or synonymised with other species.

facts.statement: A giant Ichthyosaurus appears in Jules Verne's novel Journey to the Center of the Earth, where it fights and defeats a Plesiosaurus.
facts.quote: Un Ichthyosaurus gigante aparece en la novela de Julio Verne Viaje al centro de la Tierra donde lucha con un Plesiosaurus y gana.
